divergence_note: A tethered pod descends, checks and retreats before a package reaches the ground. Two complete treatments compare a spatial delivery area and a cutaway mechanism. This is original explanatory illustration, without previous photographic inserts.

fingerprint.palette: milky sky, sage grass, ivory pod and iron cable
fingerprint.metaphor: the package can remain above the target

captions.text: The pod can come back up.
Zipline's delivery pod lowers on a tether.
The pod evaluates the drop area and can move sideways.
If it can't identify and evaluate the target, an image goes to an operator.
If the spot is unsuitable, the pod retracts.
The proposed expansion still needs FAA approval.
An FAA draft proposes expanded deliveries around Austin and other Texas cities.
Comments are open through October eleventh.
A package descending is only half the story.
The check can pull the pod back up.

searches.query: Zipline Texas September 2026 FAA draft environmental assessment droid tether delivery
searches.finding: Found the FAA review page and Texas Docket pod story; followed the FAA page and complete194-page draft, then inspected the aircraft/pod profile illustration.
No additional candidate selected from this broad query. No factual claim in the selected packet relies on its search snippets.

searches.query: site.flyzipline.com P2 droid computer vision AI
searches.finding: Found manufacturer technology and engineering pages plus leads describing visual sensors. Those search leads did not establish a fetched primary AI claim; the employer ATS source was subsequently fetched.
Found the manufacturer March2023 P2 announcement and an IEEE Droid design lead. No footage or photograph was admitted; original geometry retained.
Found employer onboard/offboard job URLs through recruiting mirrors. Fetched the exact employer ATS onboard job JSON; body explicitly names 3D perception ML transforming multiple camera inputs.
Search batch returned Droid perception role leads; selected only the independently fetched employer ATS body for the ML/camera claim. No new asset selected.

candidates.reason: Visible physical descent, lateral movement, release and retract answer the viewer question.
Equipment profiles authenticate shape but no motion or inspected reuse licence.
Decisive words useful after mechanism; a page cannot replace the physical delivery action.
Operating-area geography cannot explain the pod decision.

visual_research.decision: Original illustrative pod geometry explains control and retraction. FAA artwork is morphology reference only; no photographic insert or prior-edition asset is used.

action_proposals.visible_action: An illustrated pod descends, steers above a target and transfers an image for review. A supported winch visibly takes in the tether to retract the retained pod from an unsuitable spot.
action_proposals.consequence: The illustrative package remains in its pod when the target fails the described criteria.
action_proposals.limits: Original explanatory geometry, not an actual aircraft, private interface, observed delivery, measured success rate or granted expansion. The operator review tray symbolizes image escalation only.
action_proposals.source_basis: The FAA draft describes winch descent, lateral control, delivery-location evaluation, operator image escalation and retraction when criteria are not met. The review notice establishes the proposed Austin operation and public deadline.

retime_evidence._why: A cut is placed at the start of the line its scene carries. That word's time is measured when the reader paused before it and modelled by syllable weight when they did not, so this counts both rather than claiming all are measured.
